node.title: Re: print variable content
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [dovah],

[doc://print] is pretty much the simplest way to print a variable*. It is printed to the currently [doc://select]ed output handle.

What is your goal? Do you want the output to look a certain way, or the code to look or act a certain way?

There are modules to output the contents of complex variables / data structures, for example [mod://Data::Dump], as follows. Note the pp function by itself prints to STDERR instead of STDOUT, if you want the latter, you have to use print pp ....

use Data::Dump 'pp'; my $age = 25; pp $age; pp { foo => "bar" }; __END__ 25 { foo => "bar" }

There's also the core module [doc://Data::Dumper], which provides similar functionality.

* Update: Oh, oops, I see, you're asking about the debugger. Then [Eily]'s [id://1171232|response] is more on point.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
